headline: Sensex plunges nearly 1,000 points as rising crude oil prices and IT sell-off drag markets

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Crude oil prices spiked near $116 per barrel, dampening market sentiment.
Heavy sell-off in IT and FMCG sectors dragged major indices down.
Investor anxiety mounted ahead of the upcoming US Federal Reserve decision.
Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) outflows continued to weigh on Indian equities.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped over 900 points while Nifty slid toward the 22,500 mark.
L&T surged 6% following a 33% year-on-year increase in Q2 net profit.
HUL reported a 4% increase in Q2 net profit to ₹2,790 crore with 7% volume growth.
Jio Platforms received three 'Buy' ratings on its listing coverage initiation.
summary: Indian benchmark indices experienced a steep sell-off today, with the Sensex falling nearly 1,000 points amid soaring crude oil prices and pressure on IT stocks. Ahead of the US Fed decision and amid ongoing FPI outflows, market sentiment remained weak. However, individual earnings driven gainers included L&T, which rallied 6% on strong Q2 profits, and HUL.
